dct_description_sm: Emergency management is an integrated approach for anticipating, planning for, responding to, and recovering from all types of emergencies in order to minimize loss of life and property. Emergency management includes four distinct but related phases: disaster mitigation, preparedness, response, and recovery. Given the anticipated impacts from climate change on all four phases of emergency management on some level in the Northwest Territories (NWT), the Government of the Northwest Territories (GNWT) decided to evaluate and better understand how climate change could affect the identification and selection of disaster mitigation strategies, the types of preparedness activities that are necessary, the execution of response operations, and the implementation of long-term recovery strategies.
